info.long_name: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of Influenza A
info.short_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of Influenza A.
info.long_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level (VAL) of Influenza A. The viral activity level is the scaled number of standard deviations above a dynamic baseline. The baseline is the 10th percentile of the log-transformed and normalized concentration values, which is calculated within a 18 month timeframe every year. This is then scaled, where e is the mathmatical constant, and x is the number of standard deviations: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">VAL = e^{x}</annotation></semantics></math> These values are categorized as very low, low, moderate, high, or very high using the following breakpoints: 1.6, 4.5, 12.2, and 20.1.
info.statement: The viral activity level of Influenza A in wastewater is {value}.
info.unit: linear scaling of log standard deviations above a baseline

info.long_name: Number of influenza hospitalizations in the National Healthcare Safety Network
info.short_description: Weekly count of influenza-associated hospital admissions reported to CDC's NHSN.
info.long_description: The National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) is the nation's most widely used healthcare-associated infection tracking system. This dataset reports preliminary and finalized weekly hospital respiratory data and metrics aggregated to national and state/territory levels. Values are available for reference dates beginning August 2020. HHS collects data from state and territorial health departments about many, but not all, hospitals in the U.S. Notably excluded from this dataset are psychiatric and rehabilitation facilities, and religious non-medical facilities.

info.long_name: Percentage of Hospital Admissions with Influenza Diagnosis
info.short_description: Estimated percentage of new hospital admissions with influenza-associated diagnoses, based on claims data from health system partners, as of the week-ending Saturday
info.long_description: This data source is based on electronic medical records and claims data about hospital admissions, provided to Delphi by health system partners. We use this inpatient data to estimate the percentage of new hospital admissions with an influenza-associated diagnosis code in a given location. Delphi publishes daily values that are already smoothed over a 7-day window, so the value reported on each week-ending Saturday is taken as the weekly figure without further averaging
info.unit: Percent of new hospital admissions, 7-day average ending Saturday

info.long_name: Weighted Percent of Visits for Influenza-Like Illness from ILINet
info.short_description: Population-weighted percentage of outpatient visits for influenza-like illness.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) reported by outpatient healthcare providers through the CDC ILINet surveillance network. ILI is defined as fever (temperature of 100F or greater) and a cough and/or sore throat without a known cause other than influenza. The weighted percentage adjusts for differences in state population sizes to provide a more representative national and regional estimate. Data are available from 1997 week 40 onward and are typically published weekly on Fridays. This data is mirrored from the CDC FluView surveillance system via the CMU Delphi Epidata API.

info.short_description: Median estimate of the effective reproduction number (Rt) for Influenza, indicating whether the epidemic is growing (Rt > 1) or declining (Rt < 1).
info.long_description: The effective reproduction number (Rt) estimates the average number of secondary infections caused by one infectious person at a given time, accounting for population immunity and interventions. Produced by CDC's Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics (CFA) using EpiNow2 (through May 2026) and hierarchical generalized additive models (HGAM) with spatial partial pooling (June 2026 onward). info.long_name: Cumulative percent of pregnant women 18-49 vaccinated
info.short_description: Percent of women 18-49 with a pregnancy this season who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date, in Vaccine Safety Datalink health systems.
info.long_description: Cumulative percent of women ages 18-49 with a pregnancy during the season who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date, from electronic health records of the integrated health systems in the Vaccine Safety Datalink (10 sites). For flu, the denominator is women pregnant at any point in the season (August through March) and the numerator counts flu vaccines received since July 1 before or during pregnancy. For RSV, the denominator is women who reached 32 weeks' gestation since September 1 and the numerator counts RSV vaccines received during pregnancy. Women stay in both numerator and denominator after the pregnancy ends, and newly identified pregnancies enter the denominator over time, so cumulative coverage can fall from one week to the next. Vaccines given outside a VSD site may be missed, so coverage may be underestimated. National only; VSD members are not a representative sample of U.S. pregnant women.

info.long_name: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of Influenza A
info.short_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of Influenza A.
info.long_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level (VAL) of Influenza A. The viral activity level is the scaled number of standard deviations above a dynamic baseline. The baseline is the 10th percentile of the log-transformed and normalized concentration values, which is calculated within a 18 month timeframe every year. This is then scaled, where e is the mathmatical constant, and x is the number of standard deviations: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">VAL = e^{x}</annotation></semantics></math> These values are categorized as very low, low, moderate, high, or very high using the following breakpoints: 1.6, 4.5, 12.2, and 20.1.
info.statement: The viral activity level of Influenza A in wastewater is {value}.
info.unit: linear scaling of log standard deviations above a baseline

info.long_name: Number of influenza hospitalizations in the National Healthcare Safety Network
info.short_description: Weekly count of influenza-associated hospital admissions reported to CDC's NHSN.
info.long_description: The National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) is the nation's most widely used healthcare-associated infection tracking system. This dataset reports preliminary and finalized weekly hospital respiratory data and metrics aggregated to national and state/territory levels. Values are available for reference dates beginning August 2020. HHS collects data from state and territorial health departments about many, but not all, hospitals in the U.S. Notably excluded from this dataset are psychiatric and rehabilitation facilities, and religious non-medical facilities.

info.long_name: Percentage of Hospital Admissions with Influenza Diagnosis
info.short_description: Estimated percentage of new hospital admissions with influenza-associated diagnoses, based on claims data from health system partners, as of the week-ending Saturday
info.long_description: This data source is based on electronic medical records and claims data about hospital admissions, provided to Delphi by health system partners. We use this inpatient data to estimate the percentage of new hospital admissions with an influenza-associated diagnosis code in a given location. Delphi publishes daily values that are already smoothed over a 7-day window, so the value reported on each week-ending Saturday is taken as the weekly figure without further averaging
info.unit: Percent of new hospital admissions, 7-day average ending Saturday

info.long_name: Weighted Percent of Visits for Influenza-Like Illness from ILINet
info.short_description: Population-weighted percentage of outpatient visits for influenza-like illness.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) reported by outpatient healthcare providers through the CDC ILINet surveillance network. ILI is defined as fever (temperature of 100F or greater) and a cough and/or sore throat without a known cause other than influenza. The weighted percentage adjusts for differences in state population sizes to provide a more representative national and regional estimate. Data are available from 1997 week 40 onward and are typically published weekly on Fridays. This data is mirrored from the CDC FluView surveillance system via the CMU Delphi Epidata API.
info.statement: In {location}, {value}% of outpatient visits were for influenza-like illness.

info.long_name: Cumulative percent vaccinated against influenza
info.short_description: Percent of the population vaccinated against flu, cumulative from July through the month (or for the season / calendar year).
info.long_description: Weighted survey estimate of the percent of the population who had received a seasonal influenza vaccine since July 1, cumulative through the end of the month. Children 6 months-17 years come from the National Immunization Survey-Flu (parent report); adults 18 and older come from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (self report); the >=6 Months group combines the two. These are CDC's final post-season estimates from FluVaxView Interactive, published each fall and recalculated for recent seasons with consistent imputation methods, so they can differ from the weekly in-season dashboard numbers. Every month of the season is included in data_state.csv.gz, data_region.csv.gz, and data_substate.csv.gz, so the May row is the end-of-season estimate; data_county.csv.gz has one annual BRFSS estimate for adults per county for 2018-2022; data_setting.csv.gz gives the percent of vaccinated people by place of vaccination. CDC marks estimates as not reliable (NR) when the sample is under 30, the relative standard error is over 0.3, or the confidence interval half-width is over 10; those rows are missing and flagged in suppressed_flag.

info.long_name: Cumulative percent vaccinated, survey estimate
info.short_description: Percent of the population reporting a flu vaccination this season (or ever for RSV) as of the week ending date.
info.long_description: Weighted survey estimate of the cumulative percent of the population who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date: a seasonal flu vaccine since July 1 (children, parent-reported; adults, self-reported) or, for RSV, a vaccine at any time since it became available. Estimates come from the National Immunization Survey-Flu (children) and the NIS Fall Respiratory Virus Module (adults), random-digit-dial cellular telephone surveys weighted to the population. State estimates are for the overall population only. CDC suppresses estimates with a cumulative sample under 30 or a current-week sample under 5; those rows are missing and flagged in suppressed_flag. Survey estimates tend to run higher than registry (IIS) estimates because of over-reporting.

info.short_description: Percent of the age group with at least one dose recorded in the jurisdiction's immunization information system, cumulative through the month.
info.long_description: iis_n_vaccinated divided by iis_population, as a percent. Because immunization information systems aim to capture all doses given rather than a sample, CDC publishes no confidence intervals. Completeness varies by jurisdiction and by the laws governing what providers must report, so these estimates usually run below survey (NIS) estimates. Not every jurisdiction reports: 54 did through the 2024-25 season but only about half did in 2025-26, and CDC publishes no national estimate.

Flu coverage counts vaccines received since August 1 of the season among beneficiaries 65 and older; RSV coverage counts vaccines received since August 1, 2023 among beneficiaries 75 and older with Part D. National only. Estimates reflect claims processed by the CMS data release date and exclude Medicare Advantage enrollees, who make up about half of beneficiaries.

info.long_name: Cumulative percent of pregnant women 18-49 vaccinated
info.short_description: Percent of women 18-49 with a pregnancy this season who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date, in Vaccine Safety Datalink health systems.
info.long_description: Cumulative percent of women ages 18-49 with a pregnancy during the season who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date, from electronic health records of the integrated health systems in the Vaccine Safety Datalink (10 sites). For flu, the denominator is women pregnant at any point in the season (August through March) and the numerator counts flu vaccines received since July 1 before or during pregnancy. For RSV, the denominator is women who reached 32 weeks' gestation since September 1 and the numerator counts RSV vaccines received during pregnancy. Women stay in both numerator and denominator after the pregnancy ends, and newly identified pregnancies enter the denominator over time, so cumulative coverage can fall from one week to the next. Vaccines given outside a VSD site may be missed, so coverage may be underestimated. National only; VSD members are not a representative sample of U.S. pregnant women.
info.statement: {value}% of pregnant women in VSD health systems had received the vaccine as of {time}
